title: Introduction to Machine Learning
text:
This course introduces machine learning, covering supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and applications like transformers and large language models. It combines theory, coding, and projects to build practical skills.

Academic integrity is crucial. All work must be your own, and AI tools must be cited if used. The course emphasizes learning and applying ML in engineering contexts.

The course blends ML theory, coding cases, and projects. You'll need a strong foundation in probability, linear algebra, and calculus to understand and apply ML algorithms.

Machine learning is a field that enables computers to learn without explicit programming, using data and mathematical models to improve performance over time.

Machine learning is used in smart assistants, advertising, and electrical load prediction. These applications show how ML can solve complex real-world problems.

ML offers high efficiency, helps understand cognitive science, reduces computation time, and allows discovery of new knowledge from existing data.

Machine learning is a subset of AI that uses mathematical models and data to help computers learn. Deep learning, a more advanced form, relies on data representation rather than explicit algorithms.

Supervised learning uses training data with desired outputs. It includes regression, which predicts continuous values, and classification, which assigns discrete labels.

Unsupervised learning deals with data without desired outputs. It includes clustering, which groups data based on similarities, and dimensionality reduction, which simplifies data.

Machine learning involves inputs, outputs, and a target function. The process includes data, a model class, and an objective function to guide learning.

Every ML algorithm has three main components: representation (model class), evaluation (objective function), and optimization (search methods).

An example of ML is playing a video game like Super Mario. The model uses reinforcement learning, with an objective function to maximize coin value and optimization techniques to improve performance.
